## At a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| **Input** | 500 µL frozen airbrushed homogenate (host supernatant used) |
| **Output** | TAC in µM copper-reducing equivalents (uric acid equivalents), normalized to protein |
| **Kit** | Cell Biolabs OxiSelect Total Antioxidant Capacity Assay Kit, STA-360 ([manual](https://www.cellbiolabs.com/sites/default/files/STA-360-total-antioxidant-capacity-assay-kit.pdf)) |
| **Time** | ~1 h for one plate (estimate) |
| **Tested on** | *Porites astreoides* adults |

Antioxidants in the sample reduce Cu²⁺ to Cu⁺, which forms a coloured complex read at 490 nm. Absorbance is read before and after copper is added; the difference is compared to uric acid standards.

## Materials

- OxiSelect TAC kit (reaction buffer, copper ion reagent, stop solution, uric acid)
- 1 M NaOH, 1× PBS, DI water
- Refrigerated centrifuge, 96-well plate, plate reader at 490 nm, orbital shaker, multichannel pipette

## Solutions to prepare

Store prepared reagents at 4 °C for up to 3 months.

| Solution | Recipe |
|---|---|
| **1× reaction buffer** (1:100) | 400 µL reaction buffer + 39.6 mL 1× PBS |
| **1× copper ion reagent** (1:100) | 1 mL copper ion reagent concentrate + 99 mL DI water |
| **1× stop solution** (1:10) | 1.5 mL stop solution + 13.5 mL DI water |
| **Uric acid, 2 mM** | Dissolve 10 mg uric acid in 1 mL 1 M NaOH (≈ 60 mM), then 100 µL + 2.9 mL DI water |

Make the standard curve by serial dilution of the 2 mM uric acid, following the kit manual:

![Uric acid standard dilutions used in the 2019 run](/images/TAC_Standard.png){fig-alt="Table of uric acid standard dilutions"}

## Procedure

### A. Samples

1. Thaw 500 µL homogenates on ice.
2. Spin **5,200 rpm, 5 min, 4 °C** to pellet symbionts.
3. Split the supernatant: **100 µL for TAC**, **400 µL for protein** ([Total protein](total-protein-bca.qmd)). Keep on ice.

### B. Assay

4. Add **20 µL** standard or sample per well, in duplicate.
5. Add **180 µL 1× reaction buffer** with a multichannel and pipette-mix.
6. **Initial read** at **490 nm**.
7. Add **50 µL 1× copper ion reagent**. Incubate **5 min** at room temperature on an orbital shaker.
8. Add **50 µL 1× stop solution**.
9. **Final read** at **490 nm**.

### C. Calculate

10. ΔA490 = final − initial for every well. Subtract the blank.
11. Fit the uric acid standard curve and calculate µM uric acid equivalents. Convert to µM copper-reducing equivalents (CRE) with the conversion factor given in the kit manual.
12. Normalize to protein from the same homogenate.

## Plate layout

In the 2019 run, 8 standards in duplicate filled row A and the start of row B, leaving room for 40 samples in duplicate. Two of the kit's standards were dropped to fit all samples on one plate ([2019-11-26](../notebook/2019-11-26-total-antioxidant-capacity-porites-june-patch-adult-tissues.md)).

## Troubleshooting

| Problem | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Uric acid won't dissolve | Needs a basic solution | Dissolve in 1 M NaOH before diluting in water |
| Sample above the top standard | High antioxidant content | Dilute in 1× PBS and re-run |
